messages:
jill-customer: Hey team — our CI started failing when trying to `go get` the Go SDK after we pushed a v2 tag. Error: "module declares its path as: github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2; want github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk"
priya-support: That error screams a v2 import path mismatch. Can you paste the consumer repo's go.mod + the dependency's go.mod? Also are you hitting a private proxy or GOPRIVATE?
sam-eng: Quick check: if the upstream module has `module github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2` then consumers must `require github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2 v2.x.x` and import the `/v2` path in code.
jill-customer: Consumer go.mod snippet they run in CI: ```
module github.com/myorg/service

require github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk v2.3.0
```
li-devex: There’s the issue — the require is missing `/v2`. If their code imports `github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2` the resolver sees a mismatch.
priya-support: Also asked if they use a `replace` in CI to point at a local fork. If they have `replace github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk => ../redwood-go-sdk` that will break for v2; it must be `replace github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2 => ../redwood-go-sdk`.
jill-customer: CI logs also showed a 401 when attempting to fetch from our private proxy earlier. So they might be hitting both a path mismatch and an auth issue.
sam-eng: For the 401: ensure the CI runner has credentials for the proxy or git host. Typical fixes: set `GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme/*`, configure `GOPROXY` to the internal proxy with creds, or add a git credential helper/token. Example commands we ask in repro: 
```bash
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme/*
# if using company proxy: go env -w GOPROXY=https://proxy.internal.company
# fallback: git credential setup for https://github.com
```
li-devex: Repro checklist to send customer (minimal commands they can paste output for):
1) `go env`
2) `cat go.mod` from their repo
3) `go list -m -json github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2` (or `-m all`)
4) `git -C $(go env GOPATH 2>/dev/null || echo .) ls-remote --tags https://github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk` or `git tag -l` in vendor/fork
5) `GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme/* go get github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2@v2.3.0` and paste output
priya-support: Suggested quick mitigations to paste in the ticket:
- Update consumer go.mod to: `require github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2 v2.3.0` and change imports to `github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2`.
- If using replace, use full path: `replace github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2 => ../redwood-go-sdk` and ensure the local module's go.mod has `module github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2`.
- If they can’t change code now: vendor the dependency (`go mod vendor`) or use a temporary fork that matches the module path (not recommended long-term).
priya-support: Also asked them to try `GOWORK=off go get github.com/acme/redwood-go-sdk/v2@v2.3.0` if they use a go.work file — go.work can mask module path resolution issues.
sam-eng: Don't forget `GONOSUMDB`/`GOSUMDB` config for private modules; CI can fail if the sumdb tries to verify private modules. Example: `GONOSUMDB=github.com/acme/*` or set `GOSUMDB=off` for CI ephemeral runs.
jill-customer: I've DM'd them the checklist. They returned `go env` + logs showing both the path mismatch and a 401 from the proxy.
li-devex: For our internal releases: we should add a release-lint that validates tagged major == module path major. If someone tags `v2.x` we must ensure the module path in go.mod contains `/v2`.
deploybot: CI: added `release/check-module-path` job that compares `module` in go.mod with semver tag. Failing PRs that create mismatched tags now (:white_check_mark:).
priya-support: I'm going to provide the customer a step-by-step remediation with exact go.mod diffs and auth env vars to set. Will follow up when they confirm fixes.
sam-eng: Also log for eng: if customers keep using replace shims in CI, document the correct replace syntax in our docs and include a short note in the SDK README about v2 module path expectations.
jill-customer: Thanks everyone. I'll circle back when the customer reruns CI.
